# Pair-rotation locality test at L = 3 pairs (A F A F A F)

**Question.** Is the even-bridge bra reachable by a *few* transfer-matrix words acting on pair 1 only, with universal coefficients, at L = 3 pairs? Reference ⟨W_a^{⊗L}|, W_a = (e₁ + a e₄)⊗(e₄ − a e₁), a = 1/3 (non-good: u·Λv = a(z₄ − z₁) ≠ 0). Targets: **T1** = W_{a′}⊗W_a^{⊗(L−1)}, a′ ∈ {−2/3, 0, 2/3, 5/4}; **T2** = ((e₁+ae₄)(1−κΛ))⊗((e₄−ae₁)(1−κΛ)⁻¹)⊗W_a^{⊗(L−1)}, κ ∈ {1/3, −2/5, 5/3}; **T3** (known reachable controls) = v(1−κΛ⁻¹)⊗u⊗rest (T3a) and vΛ⁻¹⊗u(α+βΛ)⊗rest (T3b).

> **STATUS — read first (2026-10-12).** The Wolfram Engine licence expired while this notebook was being written (the shared kernel died, could not be restarted). **No Wolfram cell below has been run**: they are a faithful but *untested* port of the python computation, ready to rerun after the licence is renewed (expected outputs are quoted in the markdown under each cell; no stored outputs). **Every number in the markdown cells comes from python** (numpy; exact modular arithmetic mod p = 4194301, cross-checked with p = 4189277; python `Fraction` exact rational arithmetic; mpmath at 30 digits). Python sources: `…/scratchpad/locality/` of session 794786d6 (lib.py = transfer matrices, modlib.py/cyc.py = exact modular spans, words.py/pipeline.py = word lists) — copy them out if you want to keep them. All Wolfram symbols are prefixed `lc`.

## Verdict

**Not locally reachable.** (i) The exact span of *all* words with ≤ 3 factors t_a(θ_s + m h), a = 1,2,3, s = 1,2, m = −4..4 (48 non-zero factors; includes the task classes A·F·F, A·A·F, the inverse t₁(θ₁)⁻¹, t₁(θ₂)⁻¹ words and the 4-factor (1, t₁(θ₁)^±1)×t₁t₂t₃(θ₂-shifts) class) is 400-dimensional at L = 3; its subspace of bras of the form x⊗W_a^{⊗2} is only **4-dimensional (6 at L = 2)** and contains neither T1 nor T2 (exact, two primes, three θ-points). (ii) T1/T2 first appear at word length **ℓ = 4 at L = 3 (ℓ = 2 at L = 2)**: the span jumps 400 → 563, localised dimension 4 → 6; with *all* 48 inverse factors allowed: single-factor words (97) suffice at L = 2 (rank 54, loc 6) but not at L = 3 (rank 61, loc 3), words of length 2 with one inverse (2401) reach everything (588): the needed length grows with L either way. (iii) Even at L = 2 there is no sparse solution (no ≤ 4-word solution in the 105-word family |m| ≤ 1, L1/OMP/backward elimination give ≈ full-rank supports). (iv) What *is* local and universal: four SoV-type words {1, t₃(θ₁−h), t₃(θ₁−h)t₁(θ₂), t₁(θ₂)} and the T3 controls, with coefficients that are products of explicit per-pair θ-factors; T1 and T2 reduce **exactly** to these four words **plus the isolated pair singlet S⊗W_a^{⊗(L−1)}**, and isolating S costs ℓ = 2(L−1) factors with dense coefficients.

## Conventions and algorithm

Chain A F A F A F (site 1 = A), bras are row vectors, ψ·M. Lax 𝓛_A = (u−θ) + hK, 𝓛_F = (u−θ) − hP on aux⊗site; T(u) = 𝓛₁⋯𝓛_{2L} (site 1 leftmost), twist on the right, diagonal twist Λ = diag(z). t₁ = tr(T Λ); t₂ = ∏g⁽²⁾ tr[𝓛⁽²⁾₁⋯ ∧²Λ] (6-dim aux, F shifted by h, g⁽²⁾_A = u−θ−h, g⁽²⁾_F = u−θ); t₃ = ∏g tr[𝓛̄₁⋯ det Λ·Λ^{−T}] (𝓛̄_A = (u−θ+h) − hP, 𝓛̄_F = (u−θ−3h) + hK). Point: h = 1/2, θ = (2/7, −3/5, 8/11, −11/8, 5/13, −7/9), z = (3/2, 5/4, 2/3, 4/7); second point θ′ = (1/3, −2/5, 3/4, −5/4, 2/9, −7/10) — **non-generic**: θ₃ − θ₄ = 4h (cyclic dimensions 48/534 instead of the generic 54/588; layer structure unchanged); third, generic point θ″ = (19/23, 34/29, 41/40, −19/12, −7/11, 13/17).

All spans/ranks/memberships are done **exactly modulo a prime p < 2²²** (all entries are integers < 2²², every contraction has ≤ 24 terms, so machine doubles are exact; `Mod` after every site). The pass is the one-pass vector form (Φ[i,k] = ψδ_ik, Φ′[i,l] = Σ_{k,a} Φ[i,k][..a..]·Lax[k,l,a,b], trace with the diagonal twist). Calibration: ⟨W_a^{⊗L}|t₁(θ₁)⁻¹ = c₁⟨W_a^{⊗L}|ρ₁(Λ⁻¹) holds exactly for W_a^{⊗L} (a global rotation of the vacuum) but **not** for an arbitrary product bra, not even for W_{a′}⊗W_a^{⊗(L−1)} (the task text “any product bra” must be read as “any globally rotated vacuum”).

## Word lists (pair 1 only)

Factors t_a(θ_s + m h), a = 1,2,3, s = 1 (A site of pair 1), 2 (F site of pair 1), m = −4..4: 54, of which 6 vanish identically (zeros of the site prefactors g: t₂(θ_A+h), t₂(θ_F), t₃(θ_A+h), t₃(θ_A+2h), t₃(θ_F), t₃(θ_F+h)) → **48 factors** (24 per site, same list at 4 and 6 sites). Words commute, so a word is a multiset. Sizes: ≤ 2 factors 1 + 48 + 1176 = **1225**; triples A·F·F 24·300 = 7200, A·A·F 7200 (**task classes: 15625 words**), A·A·A and F·F·F 2600 each (all types ≤ 3 factors: 20825); four-factor class (1, t₁(θ₁)^±1)×t₁(θ₂+m₁h)t₂(θ₂+m₂h)t₃(θ₂+m₃h): 9·8·7 = 504 triples × 3 = 1512 words. Inverses: ψ₀·t₁(θ₁)⁻¹ = c₁ψ₀ρ₁(Λ⁻¹) is explicit (exact); every other inverse (incl. t₁(θ₂)⁻¹, all 48) is handled inside the exact cyclic space (an invertible operator restricted to a finite-dimensional invariant subspace has an inverse that is a polynomial in it). `lcLayers` below computes the layered span V_ℓ = span of all words with ≤ ℓ factors, the dimension of its *localised* part V_ℓ ∩ (C¹⁶⊗W_a^{⊗(L−1)}) (bras x⊗w₀ on pair 1; rank–nullity of ψ ↦ ψ(1 − w₀w₀ᵀ/w₀·w₀) on the 16×4^{L−1} reshape) and membership of each target.

### L = 2 pairs (4 sites)
Exact modular layered spans (a few seconds to minutes).

lcRes2 = lcLayers[Take[lcThStd, 4], 6];
lcLayerGrid[lcRes2]

**Expected output (python, exact mod p; L = 2 pairs):**

| ℓ | rank V_ℓ | dim loc | all T1 | all T2 | all T3a |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 1 | no | no | no |
| 1 | 11 | 3 | no | no | **yes** |
| 2 | 41 | **6** | **yes** | **yes** | yes |
| 3 | 53 | 6 | yes | yes | yes |
| 4 | 54 | 6 | yes | yes | yes |
| 5 | 54 | 6 | yes | yes | yes |

(T3b = vΛ⁻¹⊗u(α+βΛ) enters at ℓ = 2.) The full orbit of ψ₀ under the algebra generated by all t_a(u) (Krylov, generic element, two primes) is 54-dimensional, loc = 6, everything reachable. Same numbers at θ″ (generic); at θ′: ranks 1, 10, 36, 47, 48.

## L = 3 pairs (4096-dim)

`lcLayers[lcThStd, 3]` (≤ 3 factors) takes a few minutes per layer; ℓ = 4 (rank 563) needs ≈ 48·400 vector passes and 48 modular row reductions of ≈ 1000 × 4096 matrices — run it asynchronously. **Expected output (python, exact mod p; identical with p = 4189277 and at θ″):**

| ℓ | rank V_ℓ | dim loc | all T1 | all T2 | all T3a / T3b |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 1 | no | no | no |
| 1 | 17 | 3 | no | no | yes / no |
| 2 | 117 | **4** | no | no | yes / yes |
| 3 | 400 | **4** | **no** | **no** | yes / yes |
| 4 | 563 | **6** | **yes** | **yes** | yes / yes |
| 5 | 587 | 6 | yes | yes | yes |
| 6 | 588 | 6 | yes | yes | yes |

Full orbit of ψ₀ (Krylov): **588**, loc 6. At θ′ (non-generic): 1, 16, 106, 359, 510, 533, 534; at θ″: identical to the standard point. Word classes (task classes, 4-factor class, inverse words) are tabulated in the next cell.

Which factors are needed (first ℓ with T1,T2, L = 2 / L = 3): all 48: 2 / 4; A-site only (24): 2 / 4; F-site only (24): 2 / 4; |m| ≤ 1 (13): 2 / 4; m ∈ {−1,0} (10): 2 / 4; t₁ only or t₃ only: never; t₂ only: 4 / 6; (t₁,t₃): 4 / 6; (t₁,t₂), (t₂,t₃): 3 / 5.

lcRes3 = lcLayers[lcThStd, 3];
lcLayerGrid[lcRes3]

**Word classes incl. inverses and the 4-factor class (python, exact mod p, in the cyclic space; rank / dim loc / T1,T2 reachable):**

| word set | L = 2 | L = 3 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 + 48 positive singles | 11 / 3 / no | 17 / 3 / no |
| 1 + 48 inverse singles t_f⁻¹ | 49 / 3 / no | 49 / 3 / no |
| 1 + positive singles + inverse singles (97 words) | 54 / 6 / **yes** | 61 / 3 / **no** |
| … + (inverse f)(single g) (2401 words) | 54 / 6 / yes | **588 / 6 / yes** |
| 1 + singles + {t₁(θ₁)⁻¹, t₁(θ₂)⁻¹}×(1, single) (task inverses) | 24 / 4 / no | 42 / 4 / no |
| ≤ 2 positive + {t₁(θ₁)⁻¹, t₁(θ₂)⁻¹}×(≤ 2) | 51 / 6 / yes | 229 / 4 / no |
| ≤ 3 positive + {t₁(θ₁)⁻¹, t₁(θ₂)⁻¹}×(≤ 2) | 53 / 6 / yes | 400 / 4 / no |
| task classes (1225 + A·F·F + A·A·F = 15625 words); any one of A·F·F, A·A·F, A·A·A, F·F·F alone gives the same | 53 / 6 / yes | 400 / 4 / no |
| … + 504 F-site t₁t₂t₃ products | 53 / 6 / yes | 400 / 4 / no |
| … + ×t₁(θ₁), ×t₁(θ₁)⁻¹, both (4-factor ∧³-candidate class) | 54 / 6 / yes | 454, 454, 506 / 4 / **no** |
| ≤ 2 positive + all 48 inverses ×(1, single) (3577 words) | 54 / 6 / yes | **588 / 6 / yes** |
| inverses of t₁ only / t₂ only / t₃ only / A-site only / F-site only / m = 0 only, ×(1, single) | | 296 / 232 / 269 / 385 / 385 / 72, loc 3–4, no |

Caveat: t_f⁻¹ψ₀ is *not* local for generic f (e.g. t₁(θ₂)⁻¹ψ₀ ∝ ψ₀R₂₁⁻¹G₂⁻¹R₂₄⁻¹R₂₃⁻¹ moves the F-site vector onto site 4); only t₁(θ₁)⁻¹ is explicit. Inverse words must be treated exactly: a double-precision run of the L = 2 all-inverse span gave rank 50–52 instead of 54 and spurious non-membership.

**Reduction of T1, T2 to one missing vector** (exact mod p, 4 and 6 sites, three θ-points; python): rank of the four words = 4, adding S⊗w₀ gives 5, S⊗w₀ ∉ span(4 words), **T1 and T2 ∉ span(4 words) but ∈ span(4 words + S⊗w₀) for all values**. Explicit (python Fractions, a = 1/3, standard θ), in the basis {ψ₀, t₃(θ₁−h), t₃(θ₁−h)t₁(θ₂), t₁(θ₂), S⊗w₀}: the coefficients of T1(a′) are quadratic polynomials in a′ — ψ₀: 9(8a′−7)²/169 and S⊗w₀: 35(3a′−1)(8a′−7)/806 are **identical at L = 2 and L = 3**, the three word coefficients are ∝ (3a′−1)(8a′−7), (3a′−1)², (3a′−1)(8a′−7) times L-dependent per-pair constants (e.g. t₁(θ₂): 588000/382447 (L=2), 4134375/853151 (L=3), t₃(θ₁−h)t₁(θ₂): 1.2·10²¹/3.5·10¹⁸ vs 2.0·10²⁵/6.6·10²⁰ …); T2(κ)·(1−κz₁)(1−κz₄) has coefficients (29κ−14)²/196 (ψ₀), κ(29κ−14) × consts (t₃, t₁(θ₂), S: 65κ(29κ−14)/5208), κ² × const (t₃t₁) — polynomial in κ of degree 2, the same word set for all κ, L-dependence only in the per-pair constants of the four words.

**Full cyclic space (any shifts, any powers, inverses):** Krylov space of a generic element M = t₁(u₁) + c₂t₂(u₂) + c₃t₃(u₃) of the algebra (random rational u's, random c's mod p). **Expected output (python, two primes, three θ-points):** 4 sites: cyclic dimension 54, dim loc 6, all T1, T2, T3a in the span; 6 sites: cyclic dimension **588**, dim loc **6**, all T1, T2, T3a in the span. (θ′: 48 and 534.) So at L = 3 the targets *are* reachable by transfer-matrix polynomials, but only of degree ≥ 4 in the pair-1 words.

## Sparse solutions (L = 2 pairs: the only length where few-factor words reach T1, T2) — python, float coordinates in the 41-dim span, results checked exactly where stated

* Residual of T1, T2 in span(1225 words, rank 41): ≈ 1e-15 (all 7 targets); in span(1 + 48 singles, rank 11): 1.7e-2 … 6.3e-1.
* **Sparsity:** L1 minimisation (HiGHS, unit-norm columns) returns support 41 = rank for T1, T2, for the pure F-site rotation v⊗uΛ⊗w₀ and for the singlet S⊗w₀ (pool: the 1225 words ≤ 2 factors); iteratively re-weighted L1 stays at 41; orthogonal matching pursuit finds no solution with ≤ 12 words (pool of 17977 words incl. triples and inverses: residuals 1.1e-2 … 3.6e-1 after 12 words; ≤ 2-factor pool: 2.4e-2 … 5.5e-1 after 7 words); backward elimination from the full pool (60 random orders) gives irredundant supports of 41–42 words (always a basis of V₂); exhaustive search over **all subsets with ≤ 4 words** of the 105-word family (13 factors |m| ≤ 1, ≤ 2 factors) finds **no** solution for T1, T2, the pure F-site rotation v⊗uΛ⊗w₀ or the singlet S⊗w₀ (k = 1…4: 105, 5460, 187460, 4.6·10⁶ subsets; pseudo-inverse screening, threshold 1e-7); the same exhaustive search over the 97-word pool {1, 48 singles, 48 inverse singles} (float rank 52 < exact 54, screening only) finds no ≤ 4-word solution for any T1/T2 target; the k = 5 search (96·10⁶ subsets) had not finished when this was written.
* The pieces: ρ₁(Λ⁻¹)ρ₂(Λ)ψ₀ is a **one-word** target (t₃(θ₁−h)t₁(θ₂), OMP exact with k = 1), T3a two words ({1, t₃(θ₁−h)}). The pure F-site rotation and the pair singlet (the only missing ingredients of T1/T2) have L1 support 41 and OMP residual 0.08 / 0.15 after 8 words.
* At L = 3 nothing is to be sparsified for ℓ ≤ 3 (T1, T2 ∉ span); at ℓ = 4 the span is 563-dimensional.
* Mixed-integer programming (HiGHS) for the sparsest support was attempted; the solver process died (out of memory on the shared machine) before returning, so no MIP statement is made.

## Precision control and what ran where

* **Rank/membership thresholds.** Double-precision spans are unreliable here: the word bras have column norms 1e-8…1e16 and the normalised float matrix gives 411/440 instead of the exact 400 when the cut is chosen naively (noise columns). Therefore *every* statement about ranks, localised dimensions and (non-)membership at 4 and 6 sites is the exact modular one (p = 4194301, repeated with p = 4189277 for the L = 3 layers ℓ ≤ 4 and at three θ-points; accidental rank drop probability ≲ rank/p ≈ 1e-4 per rank, and two primes agree). Float (numpy) was used only for exploration, sparse searches and the individually-localised-words scan (defect < 1e-9 of the bra norm).
* **mpmath, 30 digits, 4 sites** (exact `Fraction` bras of the 11 independent ≤ 1-factor words and 41 independent ≤ 2-factor words, modified Gram–Schmidt at dps = 30): relative residual of T1 = 0.63, 0.12, 0.090, 0.31 and T2 = 0.049, 0.017, 0.13 for ≤ 1 factor (failure is not rounding), 7e-23, 1.8e-23, 3e-24, 8e-24 (T1) and 3.4e-24, 2.8e-24, 1.9e-23 (T2) for ≤ 2 factors (success; limited by the 41-word conditioning); T3a: 5e-30 at ℓ = 1.
* **6 sites**: exact rational arithmetic (python `Fraction`, one pass 15–25 s) for the identities of the controls section (calibration with c₁, c₁₂, c₃) at three θ-points, and for the explicit coefficient expansions of T1/T2 in the 5-vector basis; exact modular for all spans. (The mpmath 30-digit single-word check at 6 sites was replaced by the stronger exact-rational one.)
* **What failed / not done**: Wolfram kernel unavailable (licence expired; all `lc` cells unrun); MIP solver crashed (memory); L = 4 pairs (65536-dim) not attempted (the claim ℓ_min = 2(L−1) rests on L = 2, 3); the zero-test of factors is exact (zeros of the prefactor g).

## Summary

| item | L = 2 pairs | L = 3 pairs |
|---|---|---|
| non-zero pair-1 factors | 48 | 48 |
| rank of span, ℓ ≤ 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | 11 / 41 / 53 / 54 | 17 / 117 / 400 / 563 |
| full orbit (Krylov) | 54 | 588 |
| localised dimension, ℓ ≤ 2 / 3 / 4 / full | 6 / 6 / 6 / 6 | 4 / 4 / 6 / 6 |
| T1, T2 first reachable at word length (positive words) | **2** | **4** |
| … with inverse factors allowed (single words incl. 48 inverses → length 2 with one inverse) | 1 | 2 |
| T3 controls (A-site rotation, A-rotation×F-rotation) | ℓ = 1, 2 (words {1,t₃(θ₁−h)}, t₃(θ₁−h)t₁(θ₂)) | same words |
| individually localised words (≤ 3 factors) | 8 | the same 8 |
| 2-word fusion relations | 10 | the same 10 |
| coefficients c₁, c₃, c₁₂, σ/α | explicit θ-products | same, one factor per added pair (σ/α unchanged) |
| T1/T2 in span(4 SoV words) | no | no |
| T1/T2 in span(4 SoV words + S⊗w₀) | yes | yes |
| sparse solution for T1/T2 | none ≤ 4 words (family |m| ≤ 1), dense otherwise | not reachable with ≤ 3 factors |

**Verdict.** At 3 pairs the even-bridge target is *not* locally reachable: not by the word list of the task (≤ 3 factors, A·F·F / A·A·F triples, t₁(θ₁)^±1, t₁(θ₂)⁻¹, the ∧³-candidate class) with any coefficients, exactly; it appears only at word length 4 (563-dim span), with dense coefficient vectors, while the locally universal part (four SoV words and the T3 controls, per-pair multiplicative coefficients) persists unchanged from L = 2 to L = 3. T1/T2 reduce exactly to these four words plus the pair singlet S⊗W_a^{⊗(L−1)}, whose isolation is exactly what the pair-1 words cannot do locally (the F-site step t₁(θ₂) always carries the singlet, σ/α = h a(z₁−z₄)/θ₁₂, and its separation needs ℓ = 2(L−1) factors at L = 2, 3). A 2603-type one-parameter pair family is therefore not available from local transfer-matrix words on non-good references.
